messages:
jordan: quick heads-up — we're proposing a change to the default SDK behavior: clients will opt into an explicit routing-policy handshake instead of implicit route negotiation. this affects python/ts/go clients and how quotas are attributed. planning to do a staged rollout + console telemetry mapping. thoughts?
sam: curious — what's the concrete user-facing change? is this the same as forcing routehint header creation? :thinking_face:
li: blocking concern: some customers rely on implicit routing to route to legacy dedicated pools. if we flip implicit -> explicit by default we could break traffic. we need a compatibility mode.
morgan: agree with li. also saw a race in py-client init where lazy-init + async event loop can drop handshake in some fast-start cases. small chance but real.
jordan: not forcing flip immediately — propose new opt-in flag `routing.handshake_mode = \"explicit\"` defaulting to current implicit for two release cycles, then switch default after warnings. we need to coordinate console UX so customers can toggle per-tenant and see telemetry.
jess: from devex POV: call it out in the changelog + automated linter in the quickstart to detect old pattern. recommend a deprecation banner in Console and a migration guide example.
sam: on quota attribution: if handshake isn't present we currently attribute to fallback routing pool which skews quota reporting. solution idea: emit a telemetry event `route.handshake.missing` sampled at 1% for GA and 10% during canary. that lets us map leakage.
li: console needs a new mapping tile. current quota dashboard groups by `route_id` only; we should add a `handshake_status` breakdown and a small sparkline showing mismatch between billed tokens and expected tokens per-route. ops & billing will love it.
morgan: quick patch for python -- for anyone testing, here's a safe shim. use it in a canary install:```py
# safe route-handshake shim
from redwood import Client
client = Client(init_route_handshake=False)
# explicit call
await client.route_handshake()
```
this avoids the lazy-init race if callers need to control timing.
jordan: shipping plan idea — phase 0: telemetry-only (emit route.handshake.* events), phase 1: opt-in flag available in SDKs + console toggle, phase 2: warn-by-default in SDKs + console deprecation banner, phase 3: flip default. each phase = 2 weeks of canary + 2 weeks of org-wide.
jess: UX detail: add a console affordance to preview per-tenant impact before flipping default (simulate attribution changes using historical data). small CTA: \"Estimate quota delta\".
sam: to implement telemetry quickly we need event schema. propose fields: `client_id`, `sdk_lang`, `handshake_present`, `route_hint`, `token_count_estimate`, `env` (canary/prod). Are we okay with those?
li: keep PII-free. no user IDs. client_id ok as internal tenant id. also add `sdk_version` so we can track how many old clients are live.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary cluster for routing-service at 2024-04-18T09:00Z (job id 8342). :robot_face:
deploy-bot: canary deploy success — routing-service v3.7.1 on canary-1, traffic shift 5%. :white_check_mark:
morgan: another gotcha: go SDK's default behavior uses env-init from `REDWOOD_ROUTE` on start; we should document precedence (explicit flag > env var > old implicit). I can add a comment in go client README.
jordan: ok next steps: 1) sam to open telemetry PR with schema + sampling config, 2) morgan to add python shim example and a test for init race, 3) jess to draft Console tile mockups and the "Estimate quota delta" flow, 4) li to compile list of customers with dedicated pools for targeted outreach. i'll write the RFC and timeline.
sam: I'll add the event names and sampling to the telemetry repo today. also want a quick E2E test to validate console tile numbers against offline replay.
jess: for the deprecation messaging, recommend soft opt-in channels: changelog, console banner, and a short in-sdk runtime warning when `handshake_mode` is still `implicit` after x days of use.
li: operational ask — what's the rollback plan if quota mapping errors spike after default flip? need automatic fallback: if route telemetry mismatch > 10% for 24h, auto-revert default and open incident.
jordan: yes — include that in the RFC. mike from SRE should own the revert automation.
morgan: I've opened a tiny PR with the python shim snippet + unit test (link: https://git.redwood/redwood/python-client/pull/912). please review.
sam: I'll draft the telemetry PR (link will follow). aiming to keep event size minimal.
jess: I'll drop an initial Figma with the tile mock and a short copy for the estimate CTA.
jordan: thanks everyone :thumbsup: i'll create RFC and calendar invites for cross-team sync next week.
li: :eyes: ping when RFC is up, will arrange customer comms once we have numbers.
